summary: Up from 6.5. Most of the variety work from V2 landed. S072 is now a track plus a TOP whip. S027b, S057b, S071b, S086b and S106b break up the long blocks. The workshop has a real reverse plate (S061/S065/S067), so S067 to S068 is no longer a jump cut. S068 holds 8.79 s, under the cap, and 120 of 122 shots now move (only the S080b shake-only insert and the S109 end card don't). Runtime is 5:50 (350.2 s) with 0 VO overlaps. The cut has become more uniform, though. Stats: 122 shots, mean 2.87 s, median 2.60, sd 1.22, min 0.90, max 8.79. Histogram: <1.2: 6 | 1.2-2: 16 | 2-3: 57 | 3-5: 35 | 5-6: 6 | 6-9: 2 | >9: 0. In reference bins: <1.5: 11 (9%) | 1.5-3: 68 (56%) | 3-5: 35 | 5-8: 7 | >8: 1. The reference is 25% / 34% / 15% / 13% / 12%. The coefficient of variation (sd/mean) is 0.42 against the reference's 1.35. 23 shots now sit at exactly 2.20 s (V2: 16). That's because the new min-respecting distribution in timeline.js clamps every shot with w<1 to the 2.2 default floor, so the w-based shortening asked for in G17 has no effect. Acts 1-2 still have no cut under 1.5 s, and the film has one shot over 8 s where the reference has 12. New variety faults: 3 INSERTs in a row (S056 → S057 → S057b, 8.4 s with no face), two TOP overheads back to back (S072b → S073, and S073 hides a Round 1 → Round 2 reset inside itself), and a 4.93 s near-static laptop insert (S079) in the middle of the panic beat. Still open: S085 4.07 s unsplit, S089 not a low angle, S102 an eye-level two-shot, and the S036-S040 field plate unchanged.

But the number of shots at exactly 2.20 rose from 16 to 23, the 2-3 s band is still 47%, and CV fell to 0.42. strengths: B35 is still reference-grade action cutting: 7 shots at a 1.3 s mean (S091 1.2 → S091b 1.0 flash → S093 1.2 → S092 1.1 → S094 1.2 → S094b 0.9 flash → S095 2.6 slow-mo). The new order puts L068 'The robot turned' on the turn.
The emotional spine breathes against the argument around it: B24 3.2 s mean → S066 5.2 / S067 5.6 / S068 8.79 holds → S069 3.5. All are marked and moving, with in-frame change.
The workshop finally has two axes. The S061/S065/S067 reverse plate (door, EXIT, shelves, whiteboard) alternates with the window wall, and S063 TOP plus S062/S065 OTS add height and depth variety.

Camera motion is effectively universal: 120/122 shots move. Standouts: the S072 track (~4000 px of travel at 1080 px/s), S076 POV push z 1→2.13, S082 TELE push 2.6→3.4, S093 overhead track, S104 480 px move, S067 pull-back.

The new cutaways do their job. S027b breaks the paper block, S086b keeps the stakes visible under L064, S106b lands the 'teach me' payoff, and S071b sets up Noah in the crowd before S082 escalates it.
Transition grammar is consistent: 6 flash-ins on power beats and 3 whips (field, hall, S072b overhead).
Runtime 5:50 with 0 VO overlaps, and dialogue cuts land on line starts (S061 cuts Noah off on L043).

issues.shot: GLOBAL (timeline.js minShot default) — 23 shots at exactly 2.20 s
issues.problem: The rhythm is more metronomic than in V2. CV is 0.42 against the reference's 1.35. 47% of shots are 2-3 s, only 9% are under 1.5 s (reference 25%), and 1 is over 8 s (reference 12%). The G10 water-fill now enforces min = b.minShot ?? 2.2 per shot, so every w<1 shortening in beats without a minShot is clamped back to 2.20 (S008, S013, S017, S018, S022, S023, S040, S048, S049, S051, S063, S070, S071, S071b, S087, S088, S096, S098, S105, S107).
issues.fix: lib/timeline.js lines 39 and 48: change the default `?? 2.2` to `?? 1.6`, so w drives length and the floor is only a safety net. Then set per-shot punch cuts with explicit min/w. act1.js: S010 {w:.5,min:1.1}, S018 {w:.6,min:1.3} ('You think?'), S023 {w:.5,min:1.2} (double-take) with S022 w 1.5, S048 {w:.6,min:1.3} (glasses slide). act3.js: S088 {w:.6,min:1.3}, S105 {w:.6,min:1.3} (bad note), S071 {w:.7,min:1.5}. Spend the time on long shots instead: S070 w 1.6 (≥3 s establish), S049 w 1.4, S096 w 1.5. Target: ≤6 shots at exactly 2.2, ≥15 under 1.5 s with at least 6 of them in Acts 1-2, CV ≥ 0.6.
